# Evidence for this task

## Common GeneID-set definition

For each Control-tissue comparison, a result row is retained only when all three conditions hold:

```python
(padj < 0.05) & (abs(log2FoldChange) > 1) & (baseMean >= 10)
```

The retained rows are grouped by `comparison`, and the `GeneID` values are converted to sets. Thus a set element is a unique `GeneID`, not an un-deduplicated result row or a gene-symbol alias.

| Comparison | Unique GeneIDs after the common filter |
|---|---:|
| final blood relative to baseline blood | 846 |
| dentate gyrus relative to baseline blood | 11,663 |
| dentate gyrus relative to final blood | 11,746 |

## Three-set overlap transcription

Let:

```text
F = GeneIDs for final blood relative to baseline blood
B = GeneIDs for dentate gyrus relative to baseline blood
D = GeneIDs for dentate gyrus relative to final blood
```

The archived three-set output contains these region counts:

| Mutually exclusive region | GeneID count |
|---|---:|
| F only | 37 |
| B only | 766 |
| D only | 773 |
| in both B and D but not F | 10,316 |
| in F, B, and D | 429 |

“Across all comparisons” denotes the strict set intersection \(F \cap B \cap D\), not the union and not any two-set overlap.

## Interpretation boundary

The upstream workflow rescaled normalized floating-point expression values gene-wise and rounded them to integer pseudo-counts. These set sizes reproduce that archived exploratory output descriptively; they are not formally calibrated DESeq2 inference from raw sequencing counts.

# Shared tissue-responsive genes in a rounded-expression reconstruction of control-mouse RNA sequencing

Ondřej Veselý, Camille Dupré, Noriko Abe, and Jamal Essien

## Abstract

Cross-tissue contrasts can reveal a conserved transcriptional component even when only normalized legacy expression values remain available. We reconstructed integer pseudo-counts from archived control-mouse profiles by gene-wise million scaling and rounding, fitted tissue-factor models, and applied a common filter requiring adjusted significance, an absolute log2 fold change greater than one, and mean abundance of at least ten. Gene identifiers retained for final versus baseline blood, dentate gyrus versus baseline blood, and dentate gyrus versus final blood were deduplicated before set analysis. Seven hundred fourteen GeneIDs were present in all three contrasts, representing most of the final-versus-baseline blood set and a compact shared component of the two brain-related contrasts. The overlap supports a reproducible cross-tissue response signature, while the reconstructed inputs limit the analysis to descriptive comparison.

# Blood-anchored overlap of tissue-responsive genes in control mice

Alina Kessler, Koji Matsuda, Thandi Ndlovu, and Pierre Vautrin

## Abstract

We reconstructed comparison-specific GeneID sets from the archived Control-mouse pseudo-count workflow using a common adjusted-significance, fold-change, and abundance filter. Final blood versus baseline blood produced 1,024 unique identifiers, while both dentate-gyrus contrasts produced sets exceeding eleven thousand identifiers. Direct three-set comparison identified 512 GeneIDs shared by all three tissue contrasts. This common component accounted for half of the blood-contrast set and remained stable after removal of symbol aliases. The finding is descriptive because the workflow begins from rounded normalized expression rather than raw sequencing counts.
